newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end flat on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end flat on profit taking.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures gave up their early gains to end flat on Tuesday but dealers said the market remained well underpinned and was likely to head towards the 19,000 point target over the next week.
"Most people are looking towards 19,000 now. It does seem to be trading steadily upwards," said a trader with a U.S. futures house.
But he added that the June Nikkei was likely to face intermediate resistance above 18,700.
"Trading was pretty thin around the 18,750 level today, and we had quite a sharp pullback before the close," he said.
The June Nikkei ended unchanged at 18,590 points after hitting a high of 18,760 on volume of 14,950 lots.

Dealers said the market was boosted early in the day by buying of financial sector stocks on the underlying cash market. The April MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 351.2 points against its opening 348.5 on volume of 1,814 lots.
May also saw an increase in interest, ending at 348.6 against 346.5 on 1,244 lots.
Dealers said there was interest from both locals and institutions as Taipei stocks gained ground, partly on strength in the electronics sector. -- Sonali Desai (65-8703090)
